decisions.title: CSV grammar delegates to Go encoding/csv
decisions.issue: RFC 4180 documents a common CSV format while Go encoding/csv intentionally accepts documented deviations and exposes configurable parsing behavior.
interpretations: Delegate the complete grammar to Go encoding/csv
decisions.peer_behavior: CSV implementations differ on line endings, blank lines, bare quotes, leading space, field counts, comments, and trailing delimiters.
decisions.selected_behavior: Delegate quoting, escaped quotes, embedded delimiters, quoted newlines, line handling, and parse diagnostics to Go encoding/csv without claiming strict RFC 4180 conformance.
decisions.rationale: The standard-library parser is the observable grammar dependency and its documented deviations are more accurate than a separate partial reimplementation.
decisions.security_consequences: Malformed quoting returns classified row errors and never triggers formula evaluation or type coercion.
decisions.resource_consequences: Streaming remains incremental, with package record and field limits layered before or after delegated parsing as documented.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Go encoding/csv behavior is part of the package compatibility boundary for the pinned Go toolchain.
decisions.wire_consequences: Input bytes are parsed as text fields; this package does not emit or canonicalize CSV wire output.
decisions.upstream_status: RFC 4180 is Informational and Go encoding/csv documents its own deviations.
decisions.reconsider_when: Go encoding/csv changes observable grammar or a new CSV standard is adopted.

decisions.title: Delimited profiles and bounded logical records
decisions.issue: RFC 4180 does not define alternate delimiters, comments, lazy quotes, leading-space trimming, or pre-allocation logical-record limits.
interpretations: Expose explicit parser options and deterministic limits
decisions.peer_behavior: Delimited-text tools commonly auto-detect separators and disagree on comments, whitespace, and malformed quote recovery.
decisions.selected_behavior: NewCSVReader always selects comma; NewDelimitedReader requires one valid explicit rune; comments, lazy quotes, trimming, shape, and zero-or-positive limits are caller-selected and never auto-detected.
decisions.rationale: Explicit profiles avoid locale guessing and make permissive behavior visible at construction.
decisions.security_consequences: The record observer follows the configured quote and comment state so limits cannot be bypassed by multiline records.
decisions.resource_consequences: MaxRecordBytes is enforced before parser amplification and MaxFieldBytes before normalization; zero preserves legacy unbounded behavior.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Semicolon and other one-rune profiles remain supported only through explicit configuration.
decisions.wire_consequences: Delimiter, comment, quote, and whitespace bytes retain the delegated Go parser meaning selected by the caller.
decisions.upstream_status: These profile and limit choices are repository policy, not RFC 4180 requirements.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported standard defines dialect discovery or resource-limit semantics.

decisions.title: Headers, row shape, and normalization are repository policy
decisions.issue: RFC 4180 permits an optional header and recommends consistent field counts but does not define header normalization, duplicate handling, empty substitution, or caller-visible row policy.
interpretations: Make header, shape, and normalization policy explicit
decisions.peer_behavior: Import tools differ on implicit headers, duplicate names, short rows, whitespace trimming, and empty-value replacement.
decisions.selected_behavior: Headers are consumed only when configured; normalization returns owned copies; fixed or variable row shape is explicit; empty, duplicate, and case policies are repository-owned behavior.
decisions.rationale: Schema-like import policy is application behavior and must not be presented as CSV syntax.
decisions.security_consequences: Duplicate or empty headers can fail before downstream name-based mapping when callers select strict policy.
decisions.resource_consequences: Header and row copies are bounded by the same record and field limits as their source records.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Default readers do not consume a header or normalize field values.
decisions.wire_consequences: Normalization changes returned strings only and never rewrites source bytes.
decisions.upstream_status: Only header presence and consistent field-count guidance come from RFC 4180; normalization is local policy.
decisions.reconsider_when: Public header or normalization compatibility changes.

decisions.title: XLS requires an OLE compound Workbook stream
decisions.section: Compound File sectors, directory entries, and streams
decisions.issue: Legacy XLS is stored in an OLE compound file whose sector chains, directory entries, stream names, and truncation failures can be recovered permissively or rejected.
interpretations: Search arbitrary bytes for BIFF records
Require a valid bounded Workbook or Book stream
decisions.peer_behavior: Legacy XLS readers vary in best-effort recovery, accepted stream names, and malformed chain handling.
decisions.selected_behavior: Require a valid OLE2 compound file and exact Workbook or Book stream, reject malformed or cyclic allocation chains, and grant no macro or embedded-object semantics.
decisions.rationale: The container boundary must be validated before BIFF bytes are interpreted.
decisions.security_consequences: Malformed sector graphs, unexpected streams, and embedded objects cannot escape the read-only workbook stream boundary.
decisions.resource_consequences: The complete XLS source is materialized only below MaxWorkbookBytes, then sector and stream bounds are checked before slicing.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Best-effort recovery and pre-OLE flat BIFF files are intentionally unsupported.
decisions.wire_consequences: Container bytes are never modified and only the selected workbook stream is decoded.
decisions.upstream_status: MS-CFB is pinned separately from the BIFF8 workbook specification.
decisions.reconsider_when: MS-CFB changes relevant container rules or a maintained parser replaces the internal boundary.

decisions.title: XLS supports a strict BIFF8 ingestion subset
decisions.section: Workbook globals, worksheets, SST, and cell records
decisions.issue: MS-XLS defines many BIFF versions and record families while the package exposes only rows of strings, errors, and stored-cell presence.
interpretations: Document and enforce a BIFF8 read-only subset
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained XLS readers differ on older BIFF versions, formulas, formatting, code pages, continuation recovery, and unsupported records.
decisions.selected_behavior: Accept BIFF8 workbook globals and supported row, shared-string, number, RK, blank, boolean, and error records; ignore unrelated records; reject malformed supported records; do not evaluate formulas or claim older BIFF coverage.
decisions.rationale: A narrow observable subset is safer and more accurate than best-effort feature synthesis.
decisions.security_consequences: Macros and formulas are never executed and malformed lengths or shared-string references fail explicitly.
decisions.resource_consequences: Rows expand only to observed supported cell positions under workbook, record, and field limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Unsupported formatting, formulas, charts, macros, and pre-BIFF8 files remain outside the contract.
decisions.wire_consequences: Numbers use deterministic Go string rendering; error cells reject by default or return their Excel error token when explicitly preserved.
decisions.upstream_status: The millken/xls fixture is peer-origin interoperability evidence, not normative authority or an executed differential.
decisions.reconsider_when: The supported BIFF record set, formula policy, decoding, or cell-presence contract changes.

decisions.title: XLSX value decoding delegates to pinned Excelize
decisions.section: SpreadsheetML workbook, worksheet, cell, shared-string, and relationship parts
decisions.issue: OOXML defines typed cells, formulas, styles, shared strings, relationships, and implementation notes while the package returns normalized strings.
interpretations: Delegate raw cell decoding to pinned Excelize and own only tabular policy
decisions.peer_behavior: Spreadsheet libraries differ on formula evaluation, cached values, date and style formatting, error cells, and empty trailing cells.
decisions.selected_behavior: Delegate workbook and raw cell-value decoding to Excelize v2.11.0 with RawCellValue enabled; do not evaluate formulas or promise display formatting; apply package row, error, header, and normalization policy afterward.
decisions.rationale: Excelize is the maintained OOXML semantic dependency; this repository does not claim an independent full SpreadsheetML implementation.
decisions.security_consequences: Formula text and workbook features are data only and are never executed by the tabular layer.
decisions.resource_consequences: XLSX rows stream through Excelize after package-level ZIP, sheet, record, and field bounds are validated.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Observable raw decoding is tied to the pinned Excelize version and is reviewed on dependency updates.
decisions.wire_consequences: The package emits strings and presence bits, not OOXML; source packages are never rewritten.
decisions.upstream_status: Excelize is a production delegate, not independent differential evidence.
decisions.reconsider_when: Excelize changes raw-value behavior or the package begins owning OOXML value decoding.

decisions.title: XLSX worksheet relationships and cell presence are locally enforced
decisions.section: Workbook sheets, package relationships, and SpreadsheetML row and cell references
decisions.issue: Sheet names resolve through package relationships, while absent rows, absent cells, stored empty cells, duplicate declarations, and malformed references need deterministic tabular meaning.
interpretations: Resolve internal relationships and expose opt-in presence
decisions.peer_behavior: OOXML consumers differ on relationship recovery, sparse row padding, duplicate cell handling, and absent-versus-empty reporting.
decisions.selected_behavior: Resolve the selected worksheet through an internal worksheet relationship, reject external or malformed relationships and XML, pad missing rows and cells to observed width, and expose stored-cell presence only when explicitly enabled.
decisions.rationale: Relationship resolution owns package identity while presence is a tabular projection not supplied by the string-only delegate API.
decisions.security_consequences: External relationships, traversal targets, malformed references, duplicate metadata, and XML inconsistencies fail without external I/O.
decisions.resource_consequences: Presence parsing streams the selected worksheet a second time under ZIP, XML, row, cell, and integer bounds.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Read preserves the historical string view; ReadCells is opt-in and distinguishes stored empty cells from absent positions.
decisions.wire_consequences: Missing row numbers produce empty projected rows and cell references determine presence positions without rewriting OOXML.
decisions.upstream_status: XML well-formedness is delegated to encoding/xml; relationship and projection policy is repository-owned.
decisions.reconsider_when: OOXML relationship rules, sparse projection, or the public presence contract changes.

decisions.title: Spreadsheet packages fail closed under explicit resource policy
decisions.section: 4.3 ZIP file records and general-purpose bit flags
decisions.issue: ZIP and spreadsheet standards define representation but not application trust, decompression, path, sheet, row, cell, or diagnostic budgets.
interpretations: Apply explicit bounded fail-closed ingest policy
decisions.peer_behavior: Archive and spreadsheet readers vary on duplicate names, unsafe paths, symlinks, compression methods, expansion ratios, encrypted entries, and malformed metadata.
decisions.selected_behavior: Reject unsafe or duplicate names, symlinks when configured, unsupported or encrypted entries, over-budget sizes and ratios, malformed workbook XML, excessive sheets, rows, or fields, and invalid integer conversions before allocation or extraction.
decisions.rationale: Representation conformance does not grant authority to consume unbounded or unsafe package contents.
decisions.security_consequences: The policy bounds decompression, traversal, allocation, and diagnostic exposure and performs no network access.
decisions.resource_consequences: Workbook, archive, entry, total, ratio, sheet, record, and field limits are independent and checked at their owning boundary.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Zero values preserve documented legacy defaults or unbounded behavior; explicit limits fail with stable error kinds.
decisions.wire_consequences: Rejected packages are not partially normalized or repaired and accepted source bytes remain unchanged.
decisions.upstream_status: These resource and trust choices are repository policy layered on ZIP and spreadsheet formats.
decisions.reconsider_when: Archive support, default limits, encryption, relationship loading, or error classification changes.
